stories.summary: A simple liquid painted onto a cavity in seconds could spare thousands of kids from drilling, shots and surgery. A University of Michigan-led trial of 830 children found silver diamine fluoride stopped decay in more than half of treated baby teeth — and FDA approval as a cavity treatment may be close.
stories.extended_summary: No drill. No shots. No sedation. Just a tiny sponge-tipped applicator and a few seconds per tooth. A University of Michigan-led Phase III trial of 830 children under age 6 found that silver diamine fluoride arrested decay in more than half of treated baby teeth when applied every six months. SDF has been used for decades abroad and off-label in the US since 2014, but never with this level of large-scale US evidence — now published in JAMA Pediatrics. For the thousands of young children who end up in emergency rooms or under general anesthesia for untreated decay, this cheap, painless coating could change everything.
